tasks.label: Mobile: Prebuild Android (apply plugins)
tasks.detail: Re-applies app.json + plugins/ onto the existing android/ folder (cert pinning, release signing). Deliberately NOT --clean for routine use: a full clean wipes android/local.properties (your Android SDK path) every time, which breaks the next Gradle build unless ANDROID_HOME is set as a permanent environment variable (see certs/README.md — do this once, it's the real fix). Non-clean prebuild is idempotent and safe to re-run before every build; use 'Mobile: Full Clean Rebuild' instead if something seems stuck or a plugin change isn't taking effect.

tasks.label: Mobile: Full Clean Rebuild (troubleshooting only)
tasks.detail: Deletes and fully regenerates android/ from scratch — including android/local.properties (your Android SDK path). The next Gradle build will fail with 'SDK location not found' unless ANDROID_HOME is set as a permanent environment variable first (see certs/README.md). Only use this when troubleshooting, e.g. after adding a new native dependency or if a plugin change isn't showing up — not as a routine step before every build.

tasks.label: Mobile: Build Release AAB (Play Store)
tasks.detail: Builds the Android App Bundle (.aab) at android/app/build/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab for Play Console upload. Always runs prebuild first (see dependsOn) so it can't silently build from a stale android/ folder. NOTE: bundleRelease, not assembleRelease — Play Console requires an .aab for new apps, not a raw .apk.

tasks.label: Mobile: Build Sideload APK (local testing only — NOT for Play Store)
tasks.detail: Builds a plain .apk for directly installing on one tablet to test (adb install / file transfer), bypassing Play Store entirely. Fine for quick local testing even without release-signing env vars set (Android allows installing a debug-signed APK directly — only Play Console rejects it). Do NOT upload this file to Play Console.

tasks.label: Mobile: Export Web Build
tasks.detail: Builds the browser version of this same app into paperless_mobile/dist/ (index.html + JS bundle + assets). This alone doesn't do anything useful on its own — the backend needs a copy of it to actually serve it. Use 'Mobile: Build & Deploy Web Frontend to Backend' instead unless you specifically just want to inspect the dist/ output.

tasks.label: Mobile: Build & Deploy Web Frontend to Backend
tasks.detail: Runs the web export (see dependsOn), then clears out any previous web-dist in the sibling paperless_backend project and copies the fresh build over — assumes paperless_mobile and paperless_backend sit side by side under the same parent folder, matching how the Android build tasks above already reach into paperless_mobile. Run this BEFORE the backend's own 'Build EXE' task, which packages whatever is currently sitting in paperless_backend/web-dist into the deployed .exe/.zip — this task only stages the files, it doesn't trigger a backend build itself.
